summary: NVDA fell about 9% today (close 181.60, down from 200.13, per a Twelve Data quote) in a broad chip selloff. The only NVDA-specific new item I could find is a Reuters-sourced report that about 600,000 H200 chips sit in Hong Kong awaiting Beijing's import approval; the research already excludes China data-center compute, so it changes nothing in the research target (12m). No new SEC filing, guidance change or analyst action turned up in the window, and the other reported drivers (midterm and AI data-center rule fears, Qualcomm's handset warning) I could not verify.

items.headline: Nvidia chips stockpile in Hong Kong awaits China import approval (about 600,000 H200 chips; Beijing has not approved large-scale imports)
items.why: Opened one copy (Investing.com via Yahoo, attributing Reuters, anonymous sources; no Nvidia comment, no revenue or guidance figure). Many aggregators repeat it but I did not open the Reuters original, so the 600,000 figure is single-sourced and unverified. The supervisor's 2026-11-05 update already notes the stockpile is not in the model because NVIDIA guides no China data-center compute, so this is optionality, not a cash-flow cut: a later Beijing approval would be upside I cannot size, timing unknown, and continued refusal leaves the base case unchanged. Not a thesis trigger.

items.headline: NVDA closes 181.60, down 9.26% on the day, volume about 2.4x average (quote data)
items.why: Price move only; a price move alone is never a trigger. The close is 10.5% above the 52-week low of 164.27 and well above the 160 thesis-break level. Cause of the selloff not verified.

items.headline: Midterm fallout and fear of AI data-center rules weighing on AI stocks (themes only; no dated rule or ruling found in the window)
items.why: The only article found is dated 2026-10-22, before the window, and describes the backlash risk generally. No specific new rule, bill or ruling dated 2026-11-04 or 2026-11-05 was found in search snippets. The supervisor already lists federal AI-pause bills as not booked; this is a later, unsized threat to data-center build-out cash flows and belongs in the horizon multiple, not set aside for landing after 12 months. If a concrete rule or moratorium appears, that would be a new check.

items.headline: Qualcomm handset warning cited as a driver of the chip selloff
items.why: Could not tie any search result to a dated Qualcomm warning in the window (results were older). Even if true, it hits phone chips and memory costs, not NVDA data-center demand; the supervisor says Qualcomm input costs are already in gross margin. Unverified.

items.headline: SEC EDGAR filing list for NVIDIA (CIK 1045810): no 8-K, 10-Q or 6-K since the 10-Q cycle; latest filings are Form 4 / 4A and Form 144 (most recent 2026-10-13)
items.why: Checked the EDGAR submissions JSON: nothing filed dated 2026-11-04 or 2026-11-05, so no company filing in the window. The list can lag by a day.
